# .NET: R2R signature formatter labels Check_VirtualFunctionOverride fixups as VERIFY_VIRTUAL_FUNCTION_OVERRIDE

**Source:** [dotnet/runtime#136930](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/136930) - opened 2026-11-03 by davidwrighton (GitHub association: MEMBER; the issue body notes it was generated by GitHub Copilot from a local image inspection and source investigation - disclosed AI authorship).

## What the report says

`ILCompiler.Reflection.ReadyToRun` formats `Check_VirtualFunctionOverride` fixups as `VERIFY_VIRTUAL_FUNCTION_OVERRIDE`, which also affects tools built on its signature formatter, including R2RDump. The distinction is load-bearing for diagnosis: a failed `Check` merely rejects the precompiled method, whereas a failed `Verify` is a fatal runtime failure - so the printed label misreports the runtime contract.

The reporter observed this in a CoreCLR Wasm composite build: all five virtual-resolution checks have encoded kind `0x33` (`Check_VirtualFunctionOverride`, after masking any module-override flag) yet print `VERIFY_VIRTUAL_FUNCTION_OVERRIDE`. Expected: `0x33` prints `CHECK_...`, `0x34` prints `VERIFY_...`. The incorrect condition is also present in upstream commit `88721532dc18` and is platform-independent; no product code is affected, this is diagnostic labeling only. Stated workaround: inspect the actual fixup kind rather than trusting the formatted label.

## Verification (checked during this finding)

All three anchors check out at commit `88721532dc18` (which exists in dotnet/runtime):

- `src/coreclr/tools/aot/ILCompiler.Reflection.ReadyToRun/ReadyToRunSignature.cs`: the parser shares one case for both kinds - `case ReadyToRunFixupKind.Check_VirtualFunctionOverride:` / `case ReadyToRunFixupKind.Verify_VirtualFunctionOverride:` (lines 1409-1410) - and then picks the label with:

  ```csharp
  if (fixupType == ReadyToRunFixupKind.Check_TypeLayout)
      builder.Append(" (CHECK_VIRTUAL_FUNCTION_OVERRIDE)");
  else
      builder.Append(" (VERIFY_VIRTUAL_FUNCTION_OVERRIDE)");
  ```

  `Check_TypeLayout` cannot equal either kind handled by this case, so the `CHECK_` branch is dead and both kinds print `VERIFY_` - exactly the reported bug. The reporter's suggested condition (compare with `Check_VirtualFunctionOverride`) matches the enum.

- `src/coreclr/tools/Common/Internal/Runtime/ReadyToRunConstants.cs`: `Check_VirtualFunctionOverride = 0x33` ("If not equivalent, code will not be used") and `Verify_VirtualFunctionOverride = 0x34` ("If not equivalent, generate runtime failure") - confirming both the hex values and the semantic distinction the report relies on.

## Limits

- The five observed Wasm-build fixup entries come from the reporter's local composite image (built with the branch for dotnet/runtime#135553); I verified the formatter logic and enum, not that specific image. The mislabeling follows deterministically from the dead condition, so any R2R image with `Check_VirtualFunctionOverride` imports is affected.
- As of writing, the only comment is the repository's policy-bot triage (tooling, not maintainer assessment); no linked fix yet. The reporter's MEMBER badge reflects repository membership; the content itself is disclosed as Copilot-generated and is treated here as claims verified against source, which they are.
- Regression status is unknown per the report (the condition is old); whether any released runtime/tools version ships this formatter state was not assessed.
